seven_semantic_slots.assessment: The final theorem still concerns supplied sphere-valued X/Y and their actual expectations, with original coordinate SDE input; no abstract coupling certificate replaces them.

Scoped d,N are Nat, E=EuclideanSpace R(Fin d), S the literal norm-one subtype, C=Fin N -> S. Process time is NNReal; D/R4/L/G use Real.toNNReal. d is cast to R before subtracting 1 or 3. Borel/topological structures are induced, not arbitrary state measures.

One P and filtration precede the per-particle vector Brownian family and supplied processes. For each positive horizon the SDE event is a.e. in omega, simultaneously all t<=T,i,k and both blocks. The proof uses countably many integer horizons, not an uncountable event intersection.

Exactly the sealed hypotheses remain. Initial measurability, continuous paths, drift L1, projected noise L2, compact bounds and nonlinear Ito/centering are derived. No cross-particle independence, dimension lower bound, drift tangency, global bound, existence, or nonlinear balance premise was added. Joint measurability is retained as a source-listed redundant witness.

The actual normalized second and fourth moments and force pairing give G=L-2*lambda*(d-3)*D-lambda*R4. Continuous G, locally integrable G, oriented two-time equality, finite-horizon AC, every positive-time derivative and the within-Ici-zero derivative are proved. R4 was never changed to a squared second moment.

Input SDE equality is horizon-uniform a.e. in samples; final expectations are deterministic identities for all nonnegative endpoints, with pointwise positive-time derivatives. Only the right derivative is claimed at zero. Each horizon has its own martingale; two-time identities follow by subtraction and do not assume cross-horizon representative equality.

Fixed lambda>=0, N>0 and natural d are the only numerical parameters. All finite-horizon coefficient bounds are derived on [0,T] x C x C and may depend on T and the fields. Each paired Ito calculation uses only B_i and its literal scalar coordinates, independently of any relation between different i.

source_proof_topology_coverage.assessment: Finite product compactness bounds all full-configuration coefficient coordinates on each horizon. The bounded-progressive API proves pathwise drift L1. The exact sphere-noise constructor proves progressive L2. Initial rows are F_0 strongly measurable from strong progressivity.

The polynomial norm-square of a continuous linear difference map has explicitly derived first and second Frechet derivatives. The existing actual compact Euclidean Ito theorem is applied per particle on the image of S x S. A compact fallback comes from a supplied state and nonempty probability space, not an extra premise. Existing row continuity is transferred to supplied X/Y.

Both paired state blocks use the same Fin d driver. Their diffusion-column difference is sqrt(2lambda)(P_X-P_Y)e_j. No all-particle Brownian concatenation or cross-particle quadratic variation is used.

The column-norm sum equals 2(1-<x,y>^2). With squared chord 2(1-<x,y>), radial drift plus diffusion equals -2lambda(d-3)||x-y||^2-lambda||x-y||^4. Lambda=0 and dimension-general algebra are preserved; no Jensen substitution occurs.

Each actual zero-initial martingale is integrable and its expectation at T is zero by Martingale.setIntegral_eq. Finite sums preserve centering without independence. Time-integral and expectation linearity have explicit integrability proofs. The NNReal-to-real bridge and existing weak-balance theorem supply two-time balance by subtraction.

A countable horizon event gives global continuous full C x C paths. Weak continuity of their actual marginal law and the compact moving-law integral theorem give continuous G. Existing weak evolution gives AC; FTC gives every positive-time derivative and the within-Ici-zero derivative. No differentiation-under-expectation hypothesis is assumed.
